title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a sentence begun on the previous page (793), so the page number 191 refers to the archive scan. On page 793 Grothendieck introduces 'L.T.-groupes'. 'L' stands for 'locale' and 'T' for 'Teichmüller'. These are groups carrying a structure given by a class of mutually commensurable discrete subgroups, described as 'mixtures' of Teichmüller groups and L-groups. His illustration is an extension (6) 1 → π → 𝔊 → 𝒯 → 1, where π carries an L-structure preserved by 𝔊. Then 𝔊 is an LT-group having π as a 'subgroup of definition'. The canonical choice (7) is 𝔊 = Aut_L(π) and 𝒯 = Autext_L(π).

This page draws the conclusion: 'et ainsi le groupe [étendu?] 𝔊, extension des groupes de Teichmüller 𝒯 par le groupe à lacets π, apparaît comme un LT-groupe.' In modern terms, take π the fundamental group of a surface of type (g,n), with its 'loop structure' (the conjugacy classes of loops around the punctures). Then Aut_L(π) is the full automorphism group of π preserving this structure, and Autext_L(π) = Out_L(π) is the (extended) mapping class group, by Dehn–Nielsen–Baer. The sequence 1 → π → Aut_L(π) → Out_L(π) → 1 is exact because π has trivial centre in the hyperbolic case. This is the Birman exact sequence: the mapping class group of the surface with a marked point extends the mapping class group by π.

The point Grothendieck is making is that this extension belongs to the same axiomatic class of 'LT-groups' as the local groups and the Teichmüller groups themselves. It fits his Longue Marche programme of treating surface groups with loop structure and Teichmüller groups as a single 'tower' of groups. The next page passes to the profinite case, phrased via germs of outer homomorphisms, and to 1-dimensional algebraic multiplicities (orbicurves (U,G)).
errors: No mathematical error. The exactness of the sequence implicitly requires π to have trivial centre, i.e. hyperbolic type (2g−2+n>0); this is not stated on this page. The phrase 'les groupes de Teichmüller' (plural) refers to the whole family over all types (g,n).

ideas.what: Aut_L(π) as an extension of Autext_L(π) (the Teichmüller/mapping class group) by the surface group π
ideas.modern_name: Birman exact sequence / Dehn–Nielsen–Baer, Aut(π) ↔ mapping class group of the once-marked surface
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), discussion of discrete groups 'à lacets' and Teichmüller groups

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of 'LT-group': a group with a commensurability class of discrete 'subgroups of definition', encompassing both local (loop-structured surface) groups and Teichmüller groups and their extensions
ideas.modern_name: No standard modern notion; loosely akin to commensurators and abstract commensurability classes in mapping class group theory
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the Longue Marche manuscript (pp. 650 bis–787 continuation); not in Esquisse

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a unified axiomatic class ('LT-groups') containing surface groups with loop structure, Teichmüller groups, and the extensions between them (Aut_L(π) over Autext_L(π)). He also intends a profinite version. The notion seems not to have been developed further, here or in the literature.
missed.quote: et ainsi le groupe 𝔊, extension des groupes de Teichmüller 𝒯 par le groupe à lacets π, apparaît comme un LT-groupe.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A common framework for 'local' and 'Teichmüller' groups (discrete and profinite) could organise anabelian and Grothendieck–Teichmüller results on automorphisms of profinite mapping class groups. That work is currently done case by case.

deep.surprise_reason: The page only applies a definition to the Birman/Dehn–Nielsen–Baer extension, which is standard mathematics. The coined notion of an 'LT-group' is an undeveloped organisational idea of mild historical interest.
transcription_corrections: The group symbol is a fraktur 𝔊 (as in eq. (6)–(7) of the previous page), not \widehat{GT}. The word before it is illegible, possibly an adjective such as 'étendu'.
'par le groupe fondamental π' should more likely read 'par le groupe à lacets π' (the handwriting shows 'i/à lacets'). Grothendieck's term in the Longue Marche is 'groupe à lacets'.
'des groupes de Teichmüller' (plural) rather than 'des groupes de Teichmüller T' singular; the symbol is the script 𝒯 of eq. (6).
The final symbol is a decorative end-of-section mark, not a mathematical 𝔷/𝔍.
